title: Chapter 8 — Dasyuromorphia
description: Carnivorous marsupials of Australasia — the dasyuromorphs fill the ecological niches of small and medium predators across Australia, New Guinea, and nearby islands. The order once included the Thylacine (Tasmanian tiger), the largest marsupial carnivore of modern times, which was driven to extinction in 1936.

children.name: Sarcophilus
children.description: The Tasmanian devil — the world's largest carnivorous marsupial, and one of the most charismatic endangered animals on Earth. Devils are powerfully built scavengers and hunters with the strongest bite force relative to body size of any living mammal, capable of consuming every part of a carcass including dense bones. They are intensely social scavengers, communicating their hierarchical status with blood-curdling screams and communal feeding rituals. Mainland devils were driven extinct around 3,000 years ago following the introduction of dingoes; they survived on Tasmania where dingoes never arrived. Since 1996, devil facial tumour disease — one of only three known transmissible cancers — has killed over 80% of the Tasmanian population. Conservation breeding programs and reintroductions to mainland Australia (where dingoes have been excluded) offer hope.

children.name: Sarcophilus harrisii
children.description: The Tasmanian devil (Sarcophilus harrisii; palawa kani: purinina) is a carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

children.name: Dasyurus
children.description: Quolls — spotted, cat-like marsupial carnivores of Australia and New Guinea. Six species range from mouse-sized to cat-sized, filling ecological niches comparable to small wildcats. The spotted-tailed quoll is Australia's largest surviving native carnivore on the mainland. All four mainland quoll species have declined severely since European settlement, driven by the introduction of foxes, cats, and cane toads, and the collapse of native prey populations. Quolls are energetic hunters of mammals, birds, reptiles, and insects, and their loss has cascading effects on prey populations.

children.name: Dasyurus viverrinus
children.description: The eastern quoll (Dasyurus viverrinus, formerly known as the eastern native cat) is a medium-sized carnivorous marsupial (dasyurid), and one of six extant species of quolls.

children.name: Dasyurus maculatus
children.description: The tiger quoll (Dasyurus maculatus), also known as the spotted-tailed quoll, spotted quoll, spotted-tailed dasyure, or tiger cat, is a carnivorous marsupial of the quoll genus Dasyurus native to Australia.

children.name: Dasyurus hallucatus
children.description: The northern quoll (Dasyurus hallucatus), also known as the northern native cat, the North Australian native cat or the satanellus is a carnivorous marsupial native to Australia.

children.name: Dasyurus geoffroii
children.description: The western quoll (Dasyurus geoffroii) is Western Australia's largest endemic mammalian carnivore.

children.name: Dasyurus albopunctatus
children.description: The New Guinean quoll (Dasyurus albopunctatus), also known as the New Guinea quoll or New Guinea native cat, is a carnivorous marsupial mammal native to New Guinea..

children.name: Dasyurus spartacus
children.description: The bronze quoll (Dasyurus spartacus) is a species of quoll found only in the Trans-Fly savanna and grasslands of Papua New Guinea and South Papua in Indonesia.

children.name: Antechinus
children.description: Antechinuses — small, mouse-like marsupials of Australian forest, famous for one of the most extreme reproductive strategies of any mammal. In every species, all males die after a frenzied two-week mating season. Males suppress their immune system, stop producing blood cells, and experience the equivalent of a catastrophic cortisol-driven stress collapse — their fur falls out, they bleed internally, and they continue mating even as they are literally dying. All males are dead before the young are born. This 'suicidal reproduction' is thought to be an adaptation to a narrow window of insect abundance — with no males surviving to compete for food, the females and young have exclusive access to the peak resource.

children.name: Antechinus stuartii
children.description: The brown antechinus (Antechinus stuartii), also known as Stuart's antechinus and Macleay's marsupial mouse, is a species of small carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

children.name: Antechinus agilis
children.description: The agile antechinus (Antechinus agilis) is a species of small carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

children.name: Antechinus swainsonii
children.description: The dusky antechinus (Antechinus swainsonii), also known as Swainson's antechinus or the dusky marsupial mouse, is a species of small marsupial carnivore, a member of the family Dasyuridae.

children.name: Antechinus flavipes
children.description: The yellow-footed antechinus (Antechinus flavipes), also known as the mardo, is a shrew-like marsupial found in Australia..

children.name: Antechinus minimus
children.description: The swamp antechinus (Antechinus minimus), also known as the little Tasmanian marsupial mouse, is a species of shrew-like marsupial of the family Dasyuridae and as such is related to dunnarts, quolls and the Tasmanian devil.

children.name: Antechinus adustus
children.description: The tropical antechinus (Antechinus adustus), also known as the rusty antechinus, is a species of small marsupial carnivore, particularly closely related to the brown antechinus (Antechinus stuartii).

children.name: Antechinus godmani
children.description: The Atherton antechinus (Antechinus godmani), also known as Godman's antechinus, is a species of small carnivorous, insectivorous marsupial native to Australia.

children.name: Antechinus leo
children.description: The cinnamon antechinus (Antechinus leo), also known as the Iron Ranges antechinus and the Cape York antechinus, is a species of small carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

children.name: Antechinus billardierii
children.description: Endemic to Tasmania and its offshore islands. A robust, dark antechinus of rainforest and wet eucalypt forest. Behaviourally similar to mainland congeners but benefits from the absence of foxes and significant predator pressure on Tasmania.

children.name: Antechinus argentus
children.description: The silver-headed antechinus (Antechinus argentus) is a species of dasyurid marsupial of the genus Antechinus..

children.name: Antechinus arktos
children.description: Antechinus arktos, the black-tailed antechinus, is a species of small carnivorous marsupial native to Australia.

children.name: Antechinus mysticus
children.description: The  buff-footed antechinus (Antechinus mysticus) is a species of marsupial..

children.name: Antechinus subtropicus
children.description: The subtropical antechinus (Antechinus subtropicus) is a species of small carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

children.name: Antechinus mimetes
children.description: Separated from A. swainsonii in 2015 on the basis of genetic and morphological evidence. Occupies cool montane forests of south-eastern mainland Australia. Darker and slightly smaller than the Tasmanian dusky antechinus.

children.name: Antechinus vandycki
children.description: Antechinus vandycki, the Tasman Peninsula dusky antechinus, is a species of marsupial in the family Dasyuridae..

children.name: Sminthopsis
children.description: Dunnarts — small, mouse-like dasyurid marsupials of Australia and New Guinea, some of the smallest marsupials. Dunnarts are fierce insectivores and small vertebrate predators, with pointed snouts and large eyes. Like many small dasyurids, they store fat in their tails during periods of abundance and can enter torpor during cold nights or food shortage. The fat-tailed dunnart is a model organism in marsupial research. Several species have declined severely due to changes in fire regimes, land clearing, and introduced predators.

children.name: Sminthopsis crassicaudata
children.description: The fat-tailed dunnart (Sminthopsis crassicaudata) is a species of mouse-like marsupial of the Dasyuridae, the family that includes the little red kaluta, quolls, and the Tasmanian devil..

children.name: Sminthopsis murina
children.description: The slender-tailed dunnart (Sminthopsis murina), also known as the common dunnart in Australia, is a dasyurid marsupial..

children.name: Sminthopsis leucopus
children.description: The white-footed dunnart (Sminthopsis leucopus) is a marsupial that occurs on Tasmania and mainland Australia..

children.name: Sminthopsis macroura
children.description: The striped-faced dunnart (Sminthopsis macroura) is a small, Australian, nocturnal, "marsupial mouse," part of the family Dasyuridae..

children.name: Sminthopsis lanigera
children.description: Distinctive for its woolly, pencil-shaped tail. Endemic to south-western Western Australia, where it inhabits mallee scrub, heath, and open woodland. One of the least-studied Australian dunnarts; rarely trapped.

children.name: Sminthopsis longicaudata
children.description: The long-tailed dunnart (Antechinomys longicaudatus) is an Australian dunnart that, like the little long-tailed dunnart, has a tail longer than its body..

children.name: Sminthopsis douglasi
children.description: The Julia Creek dunnart (Sminthopsis douglasi) is a marsupial with a buffy brown upperside and white underside..

children.name: Sminthopsis aitkeni
children.description: The Kangaroo Island dunnart (Sminthopsis aitkeni) is a dark sooty-grey coloured dunnart species first described in 1969, with paler underparts of its body..

children.name: Sminthopsis psammophila
children.description: The sandhill dunnart (Sminthopsis psammophila) is a species of carnivorous Australian marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

children.name: Sminthopsis dolichura
children.description: The Little long-tailed dunnart (Sminthopsis dolichura) is a dunnart that was, along with Gilbert's dunnart, described in 1984..

children.name: Sminthopsis fuliginosus
children.description: The sooty dunnart (Sminthopsis fuliginosus) is a species of dunnart found in Western Australia.

children.name: Sminthopsis ooldea
children.description: The Ooldea dunnart (Sminthopsis ooldea), also called Troughton's dunnart after the person who found the species, is an Australian marsupial similar to the hairy-footed dunnart.

children.name: Sminthopsis hirtipes
children.description: The hairy-footed dunnart (Sminthopsis hirtipes) is a dunnart that has silver hairs on the soles of it hind feet accompanied by long hair on the side of its sole..

children.name: Sminthopsis youngsoni
children.description: The lesser hairy-footed dunnart (Sminthopsis youngsoni) is a small carnivorous Australian marsupial of the family Dasyuridae..

children.name: Sminthopsis granulipes
children.description: The white-tailed dunnart (Sminthopsis granulipes), also known as the ash-grey dunnart, is a dunnart native to Australia..

children.name: Sminthopsis gilberti
children.description: Gilbert's dunnart (Sminthopsis gilberti) is a dunnart, described in 1984..

children.name: Sminthopsis griseoventer
children.description: The grey-bellied dunnart (Sminthopsis griseoventer), alternately spelled gray-bellied dunnart, was described by Kitchener, Stoddart and Henry along with the Kangaroo Island dunnart, Gilbert's dunnart and little long-tailed dunnart in 1984..

children.name: Sminthopsis callipygus
children.description: Restricted to the Pilbara region of north-western Western Australia, where it inhabits rocky slopes and spinifex grassland. A robust dunnart with a thick-based tail. Described in 1975; among the less-studied members of the genus.

children.name: Sminthopsis butleri
children.description: The Carpentarian dunnart (Sminthopsis butleri) also known as Butler's dunnart is a marsupial with a puffy brown or mouse grey colour above and the underside of white, similar to its close relative the Kakadu dunnart.

children.name: Sminthopsis virginiae
children.description: The red-cheeked dunnart (Sminthopsis virginiae) is an Australasian marsupial so called because of the distinctive red hair on its cheek..

children.name: Sminthopsis archeri
children.description: The chestnut dunnart (Sminthopsis archeri) is a dunnart that was described by Van Dyck in 1986 and is named because of its chestnut colour in the upperparts of its body.

children.name: Sminthopsis bindi
children.description: The Kakadu dunnart (Sminthopsis bindi) is a dunnart first described in 1994 and whose closest relative is the Carpentarian dunnart.

children.name: Ningaui
children.description: Ningauis — tiny, fierce predators of arid and semi-arid Australia. Among the smallest marsupials, weighing only 2–9 g, ningauis punch well above their weight: they routinely kill prey larger than themselves, including large insects, spiders, and small lizards. The name derives from an Aboriginal Australian spirit creature. Three species occupy spinifex grassland, mulga shrubland, and heath across the continent.

children.name: Ningaui timealeyi
children.description: The Pilbara ningaui (Ningaui timealeyi), sometimes known as Ealey's ningaui, is a tiny species of marsupial carnivore found in Australia.

children.name: Ningaui ridei
children.description: The Wongai ningaui (Ningaui ridei) is a tiny carnivorous marsupial native to the arid open grasslands of inland Australia.

children.name: Ningaui yvonneae
children.description: The southern ningaui (Ningaui yvonneae) is a tiny marsupial carnivore belonging to the Dasyuridae family.

children.name: Planigale
children.description: Planigales — the flattest-headed marsupials. Their skulls are laterally compressed to allow them to pursue prey into narrow rock crevices and soil cracks — a feature so extreme that the skull of the common planigale is less than 3 mm deep. Despite weighing as little as 4 g, planigales are voracious predators of invertebrates and small lizards. Five species span Australia and New Guinea, from tropical savanna to semi-arid grassland.

children.name: Planigale maculata
children.description: The common planigale (Planigale maculata), also known as the pygmy planigale or coastal planigale, is one of the small carnivorous marsupials known as "marsupial mice" found in Australia.

children.name: Planigale ingrami
children.description: The long-tailed planigale (Planigale ingrami), also known as Ingram's planigale or the northern planigale, is the smallest of all marsupials, and one of the smallest of all mammals..

children.name: Planigale tenuirostris
children.description: The narrow-nosed planigale (Planigale tenuirostris) is a small Australian carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae..

children.name: Planigale gilesi
children.description: The paucident planigale (Planigale gilesi), also known as Giles' planigale, is a very small species of carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.

children.name: Planigale novaeguineae
children.description: The New Guinean planigale (Planigale novaeguineae), also known as the Papuan planigale, is a species of small marsupial carnivore native to the Trans-Fly savanna and grasslands of New Guinea..

children.name: Dasykaluta
children.description: A monotypic genus erected for the red-eared antechinus of the Pilbara. Dasykaluta superficially resembles an antechinus but belongs to a distinct lineage. Like the antechinuses, males are semelparous — all die after a brief annual mating season. The genus name combines Dasy- (hairy) with Kaluta, the local Aboriginal name.

children.name: Dasykaluta rosamondae
children.description: The little red kaluta (Dasykaluta rosamondae) is a small, reddish-brown, shrew-like mammal native to dry grasslands of northwest Western Australia..

children.name: Parantechinus
children.description: Parantechinuses — two species of medium-sized dasyurids from arid and semi-arid Australia. Unlike the true antechinuses, parantechinus males are not strictly semelparous: some males survive their first breeding season. Both species are rarely encountered; the dibbler is one of the most critically threatened Australian mammals.

children.name: Parantechinus apicalis
children.description: The dibbler (Parantechinus apicalis) is an endangered species of marsupial..

children.name: Parantechinus bilarni
children.description: The sandstone false antechinus (Pseudantechinus bilarni), also known as the sandstone pseudantechinus, the sandstone antechinus, the sandstone dibbler, Harney's antechinus and the Northern dibbler, is a species of small carnivorous marsupial, which has a patchy distribution in Australia's Northern Territory..

children.name: Pseudantechinus
children.description: Pseudantechinuses — six species of small, fat-tailed dasyurids of arid and rocky Australia. They store fat in the tail and can use torpor to survive lean periods. Despite resembling antechinuses, they are not closely related; males typically survive beyond the first breeding season. Several species are restricted to narrow rocky habitat and are poorly known.

children.name: Pseudantechinus macdonnellensis
children.description: The fat-tailed false antechinus (Pseudantechinus macdonnellensis), also called the fat-tailed pseudantechinus and red-eared antechinus, is a member of the order Dasyuromorphia..

children.name: Pseudantechinus ningbing
children.description: The Ningbing false antechinus (Pseudantechinus ningbing), also known as the Ningbing pseudantechinus, is a small species of carnivorous marsupial found in north-western Australia..

children.name: Pseudantechinus roryi
children.description: Rory Cooper's false antechinus (Pseudantechinus roryi), also known as the tan false antechinus and the tan pseudantechinus, is a recently named species of small carnivorous marsupial which inhabits rocky outcrops in Western Australia..

children.name: Pseudantechinus mimulus
children.description: The Alexandria false antechinus (Pseudantechinus mimulus), also known as the Carpentarian false antechinus or Carpentarian pseudantechinus, is a small carnivorous marsupial, found only in a number of small, isolated localities in northern Australia..

children.name: Pseudantechinus woolleyae
children.description: Woolley's false antechinus (Pseudantechinus woolleyae), also known as Woolley's pseudantechinus, is a species of small carnivorous marsupial belonging to the family Dasyuridae..

children.name: Pseudantechinus bilarni
children.description: The sandstone false antechinus (Pseudantechinus bilarni), also known as the sandstone pseudantechinus, the sandstone antechinus, the sandstone dibbler, Harney's antechinus and the Northern dibbler, is a species of small carnivorous marsupial, which has a patchy distribution in Australia's Northern Territory..

children.name: Dasycercus
children.description: Mulgaras — two species of mid-sized, thick-tailed dasyurids of the arid interior. One of the dominant small predators of Australian desert, mulgaras subsist entirely on live prey — insects, spiders, lizards, and small rodents — and obtain all their water from their food. Their fat-storing tail swells markedly when food is plentiful.

children.name: Dasycercus cristicauda
children.description: The crest-tailed mulgara (Dasycercus cristicauda) was a small Australian carnivorous marsupial..

children.name: Dasycercus blythi
children.description: The brush-tailed mulgara (Dasycercus blythi) is a medium sized carnivorous Australian marsupial species..

children.name: Myoictis
children.description: Three-striped dasyures of New Guinea — medium-sized forest dasyurids with distinctive dorsal striping. Myoictis species occupy primary and secondary rainforest and monsoon forest from sea level to montane zones across New Guinea and some adjacent islands. They are solitary, nocturnal predators of large invertebrates and small vertebrates.

children.name: Myoictis melas
children.description: The three-striped dasyure (Myoictis melas) is a member of the order Dasyuromorphia..

children.name: Myoictis leucura
children.description: Woolley's three-striped dasyure (Myoictis leucura) is a member of the order Dasyuromorphia..

children.name: Myoictis wallacii
children.description: Wallace's dasyure (Myoictis wallacei) or Wallace's three-striped dasyure is a member of the order Dasyuromorphia..

children.name: Myoictis wavicus
children.description: The Tate's three-striped dasyure (Myoictis wavicus) is a member of the order Dasyuromorphia..

children.name: Murexia
children.description: Short-furred dasyures of New Guinea — forest-dwelling dasyurids known from New Guinea and the Aru Islands. Murexia species are small to medium-sized nocturnal predators of the rainforest floor and understorey. The genus has been subject to repeated revision; species formerly placed in Phascolosorex and Antechinus have been moved here.

children.name: Murexia longicaudata
children.description: The short-furred dasyure (Murexia longicaudata), also known as the short-haired marsupial mouse, is a member of the order Dasyuromorphia..

children.name: Murexia rothschildi
children.description: The broad-striped dasyure (Murexia rothschildi) is a species of marsupial in the family Dasyuridae..

children.name: Phascolosorex
children.description: Marsupial shrews of New Guinea — two species of slender, shrew-like dasyurids restricted to the mountains of New Guinea above 1,000 m. The dorsal striping of Phascolosorex dorsalis makes it one of the most visually distinctive New Guinea dasyurids. Little is known of the ecology of either species.

children.name: Phascolosorex dorsalis
children.description: The narrow-striped dasyure or narrow-striped marsupial shrew (Phascolosorex dorsalis) is a species of marsupial in the family Dasyuridae found in West Papua and Papua New Guinea..

children.name: Phascolosorex doriae
children.description: The red-bellied dasyure or red-bellied marsupial shrew (Phascolosorex doriae) is a species of marsupial in the family Dasyuridae endemic to West Papua..

children.name: Neophascogale
children.description: A monotypic genus containing only the speckled dasyure of New Guinea's central mountains. Neophascogale lorentzii is one of the larger New Guinea dasyurids, distinguished by long, coarse fur and pale speckled patterning. It occupies montane forest above 1,500 m and is considered near threatened.

children.name: Neophascogale lorentzii
children.description: The speckled dasyure (Neophascogale lorentzii), also known as the long-clawed marsupial mouse, is a member of the order Dasyuromorphia.

children.name: Micromurexia
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Habbema dasyure, a very small, short-furred forest dasyurid from the highlands of West Papua. Separated from Murexia on molecular and morphological grounds; rarely collected and poorly known.

children.name: Micromurexia habbema
children.description: The Habbema dasyure (Murexia habbema) is a species of marsupial in the family Dasyuridae found in West Papua, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Phascogale
children.description: Phascogales — two species of tree-climbing, pouched dasyurids of Australian forest. Agile and acrobatic, they forage for invertebrates and small vertebrates in the bark and hollows of large eucalypts. Like the antechinuses, males are semelparous — all die after the annual mating season. The brush-tailed phascogale has one of the most spectacular tails of any marsupial: the distal third is covered in long, bushy black hairs that flare out when the animal is alarmed.

children.name: Phascogale tapoatafa
children.description: The brush-tailed phascogale (Phascogale tapoatafa), also known by its Australian native name tuan, the common wambenger, the black-tailed mousesack or the black-tailed phascogale, is a rat-sized arboreal carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae, characterized by a tuft of black silky hairs on the terminal portion of its tail..

children.name: Paramurexia
children.description: A monotypic genus for the Broad-striped dasyure of New Guinea — a medium-sized, boldly patterned forest dasyurid with a wide dark dorsal stripe. Sometimes placed in Murexia; molecular work supports its separation. Found in lowland and hill forest of Papua New Guinea.

children.name: Paramurexia rothschildi
children.description: The broad-striped dasyure (Murexia rothschildi) is a species of marsupial in the family Dasyuridae..
